title: ChurnCast: End-to-End Data Science Case Study on Subscription Churn
tagline: Take a messy meal-subscription export from raw CSVs to a tested, leakage-free churn model that beats the retention team's rule of thumb, with grouped out-of-time validation, calibration and fairness checks, CI with an evaluation gate, a prediction API with an AI explainer, and monitoring and retraining after it goes live
description: TiffinBox, a meal-subscription startup, loses about 9 % of its paying customers every month, and its retention team can call only 10 % of them with an offer. Over nine phases you build the churn model they need, like a professional data science team: frame the decision and the label, write a data contract, a timeline and a modelling plan with ADRs, then build the pipeline test-first in your track: load four deliberately messy CSVs as text, apply documented cleaning rules that count every row they drop, check the contract, build point-in-time features that only use what was known at each month-end snapshot (and avoid the leaky cancellation_reason column), compare two baselines (the training churn rate and the team's five-flag rule) with two logistic regressions using grouped 5-fold cross-validation, then evaluate the champion once on out-of-time test months: AUC, average precision, Brier, calibration (ECE), precision and recall of the top-10 % call list, net value per month, slices, an age-band fairness check and a leakage scan, all behind a release gate. Golden files, invariants, leakage and contract-violation tests pin every number, and the Python, SQL and R tracks must agree (features to 1e-9, metrics and coefficients to 1e-6). CI executes the notebook or R Markdown report, runs the gate and checks parity; a generated model card and a FastAPI prediction API with an optional AI explainer (numbered facts in, guardrails out, a deterministic template as fallback) ship in Docker as v1.0.0. Then the model meets the real world: a new acquisition channel breaks the contract, prices change, and the deployed model's calibration slips. You version the contract, add drift (PSI) and realised-performance monitoring, recalibrate and retrain a challenger, decide champion vs challenger on a holdout month, add request ids, JSON logs and Prometheus metrics to the API, and write a blameless post-mortem (v1.1.0). Pick Python (pandas, scikit-learn, Jupyter), SQL (DuckDB) or R (tidymodels, R Markdown); the data, contract, golden files and API are shared. Everything runs on a laptop with no paid service and no API key.

prerequisites.title: Git and the command line basics
One of: Python with pandas, SQL (GROUP BY, JOIN, window functions) or R with dplyr
Basic statistics and the idea of a classifier: probabilities, a train/test split, overfitting

outcomes: Frame a business request as a prediction problem: the decision, the unit, the snapshot, the label and what a wrong call costs
Write a data contract (schema, accepted values, checks with severities) and a modelling plan with ADRs before training anything
Build point-in-time features from messy event tables without leaking the future, and recognise a leaky column
Validate honestly: grouped cross-validation by customer and an out-of-time test set used once
Compare models with baselines first (prior and the team's rule of thumb), and choose a champion by a rule written in advance
Evaluate for the decision: ranking (AUC, AP), probabilities (Brier, calibration), the capacity-limited call list, value, slices and fairness
Pin a model with golden files, invariants, leakage and contract-violation tests, and make three implementations agree
Gate a release in GitHub Actions CI, generate a model card from the numbers, and serve the model with a FastAPI API in Docker
Add an AI explainer that only sees aggregate facts, is checked by guardrails and falls back to a deterministic template
Monitor a live model (PSI drift, realised performance), retrain and recalibrate a challenger, decide on a holdout and write a blameless post-mortem
Use AI assistants deliberately and verify every number they produce
ai_feature: An optional AI explainer in the prediction API: for one customer it receives only numbered facts (the churn probability, the base rate and the top feature contributions; never the customer id, raw records or a protected attribute) and writes a short note for a retention agent. Guardrails reject any answer with an unknown citation, a number that is not a correct rounding of a fact, a certainty claim ("will churn") or a sensitive attribute, and the API then returns a deterministic template instead. Offline by default; any OpenAI-compatible endpoint (a local Ollama, or a free Gemini/Groq key) can be plugged in
portfolio_blurb: Built ChurnCast, an end-to-end churn model for a meal-subscription business on a deliberately messy export (customers, invoices, usage, support tickets): a versioned data contract with severity-graded checks, counted cleaning rules, point-in-time features at month-end snapshots (with a leakage scan that caught the cancellation_reason trap), two baselines and two logistic regressions compared with grouped 5-fold cross-validation, and an out-of-time test used once. The champion (test AUC 0.743, ECE 0.008) ranks the top-10 % call list 3.0x better than random, finds 30 % of next month's churners and is worth about ₹1.1 lakh a month against ₹63,000 for the team's rule of thumb, within an age-band recall gap of 0.12. Golden files, invariants and leakage tests; Python, SQL and R implementations that agree to 1e-6; a release gate and a generated model card in GitHub Actions CI; a FastAPI prediction API in Docker with a guard-railed AI explainer; and, after deployment, PSI drift and realised-performance monitoring that flagged a miscalibrated model, a recalibrated challenger promoted on a holdout month (Brier 0.119 → 0.113, ECE 0.059 → 0.013), request ids, JSON logs, Prometheus metrics and a blameless post-mortem (v1.1).
